chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding
the poisonous lizard (samma' abras) that falls into the well. He said: 'It is not anything (of concern). Stir the water with the bucket.'

key_terms.السَّامّ أَبْرَص: A venomous white-speckled lizard/gecko; considered ritually impure (najis) upon death; the question concerns its effect on well water
key_terms.الْبِئْر: A water well; in Islamic law, well water has a large volume and specific rulings apply to its purification
key_terms.حَرِّكِ الْمَاءَ بِالدَّلْوِ: Stir the water with the bucket; a purification method by agitation, implying no removal of water is necessary
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْء: It is not anything; a formulaic dismissal indicating that no legal consequence follows from the event

ai.seo_question: Does a venomous lizard falling into a well make the water impure in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) was asked about the ritual purity of well water when a sama' abras — a type of venomous lizard — falls into it. His ruling is that the water remains pure and usable; the questioner need only stir the water with a bucket. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that well water is not easily rendered impure, especially from animal contact where no visible contamination occurs.
